title: Degree change of m-pseudo-coherence under shift by one
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $m\in\mathbf Z$, and $C\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $C[1]$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent] if and only if $C$ is $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 064R, proof of lemma-cone-pseudo-coherent, assertions (2) and (3), using shifts

proof.text: An isomorphism C -> D transports any witness by composition: functors preserve the isomorphism, so all homology isomorphisms and the boundary epimorphism are preserved.

For any integer shift n, shift a witness E -> C through degree m to E[n] -> C[n], using Q.commShiftIso. The bounds become a-n,b-n by CochainComplex.isStrictlyGE_shift and isStrictlyLE_shift. Each shifted term is isomorphic to E^{i+n}; transfer freeness with Module.Free.of_equiv and finiteness with Module.Finite.equiv. The homology shift isomorphisms Functor.shiftIso identify the shifted map in degree i with the original map in degree i+n. Naturality conjugates the maps by isomorphisms, preserving IsIso and Epi. Thus the new approximation degree is m-n.

Shift a witness for C[1] by -1 and compose with shiftFunctorCompIsoId to get a witness for C at m+1. Conversely shift a witness for C at m+1 by 1 to get a witness for C[1] at m. The integer index equalities are immediate.

theorem isMPseudoCoherent_shift_one_iff
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (m : ℤ) (C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) :
    IsMPseudoCoherent m (C⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) ↔ IsMPseudoCoherent (m + 1) C
